topic: replay_status can itself return stale or drifted data
observed: TWO capture agents independently reported it in the same session, on unrelated frames. (1) j49 2026-06-04 P3 09:29: replay_status returned 1780582979 - a cursor from a DIFFERENT trades day, ~83,100s from the expected 1780666139 - on its first check, and returned the correct value after one replay_start re-issue. (2) j49 2026-06-03 A6 10:23: data_get_ohlcv AND a subsequent replay_status both returned bars aligned to Fri 5 Jun ~09:20-09:29 while the frame was Thu 4 Jun 10:23; it self-corrected after a replay_start re-issue.
why_it_matters: the standing rule in every capture brief is 'replay_start returns a stale cursor; only replay_status is trustworthy.' That rule is now known to be incomplete - replay_status is MORE trustworthy, not infallible. A run that trusted replay_status alone, without comparing it to an independently computed expected_cursor, could have built a briefing on the wrong day's bars.
what_saved_it: the expected_cursor arithmetic. Every capture brief in this run computes the cursor from the session anchor BEFORE reading it, and instructs the agent to re-issue on mismatch. Both incidents were caught by that check on the first comparison and both resolved inside the allowed retries. The final frames were verified aligned (bar_start, delta and the study values' own visible-bar timestamps all cross-checked).
consequence_for_this_run: none - no briefing was built on a mismatched cursor. Recorded so the rule is not carried forward in its weaker form: the check is the safeguard, not the tool.
